# Results — Study 445 (Elliott Wave)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Elliott Wave Theory is **irreducibly
subjective** — the "correct" wave count is only knowable in hindsight and two analysts label the
same chart differently, so there is no single falsifiable rule. We test the **tightest mechanical
version proponents accept**: a standard **ZigZag** swing detector (5% reversal) marks the pivots,
a **Fibonacci** filter validates the wave-2 retracement, and we test the one forward-looking,
tradable claim — after a clean impulse 1-2 with a textbook wave-2 retracement, **wave 3 extends in
the impulse direction** (the entry every Elliottician wants). One-day execution lag; one-sample +
HAC *t*; a same-bars label-shuffle placebo; costs. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLC, auto-adjusted (total-return), public, no key |
| Basket | SPY, QQQ, DIA, IWM, ^GSPC, ^IXIC, ^DJI, GLD — broad indices/ETFs proponents draw waves on |
| As-of | **2025-12-31** (partial 2026 dropped — no partial year in a stamped run) |
| SPY window | 1993-01-29 → 2025-12-31 (**32.9** years, 8,288 bars), fingerprint **`7ce3202106f8`** |
| Detector | 5% percentage **ZigZag** pivots; wave-3 entry requires a wave-2 Fibonacci retracement in **38.2%–78.6%** (textbook 50–61.8% sits inside) and obeying EW rule 2 (wave 2 does not exceed wave-1 start) |
| Entry / costs | enter the close **one day after** the pivot is confirmed (no look-ahead); hold 5/10/20/40 days; **1 bp** one-way (×2 round trip) |

> **No cross-sectional survivorship sort.** These are *price-index* tapes, not a single-name
> basket, so there is no surviving-names selection on the Signal axis. The only selection is that
> we draw waves on indices that exist today — a benign, transparent choice for a method whose whole
> point is broad-index charts.

## The signal — the wave-3 prediction (pooled across the basket)

The headline is the **pooled** test (2,512 ZigZag pivots → **661** valid impulse-1-2 wave-3
entries) — pooling the eight tapes buys statistical power a single index can't. Trade direction =
the wave-1 direction; the *t* is one-sample (and HAC/Newey-West) of the directional forward return
vs 0; the placebo *p* is the share of 5,000 **same-bars random-direction shuffles** whose mean
beats the observed (the honest "does the wave count beat a coin at the same swing points?").

| horizon | n | gross (bps) | net (bps) | win-rate | one-sample *t* | HAC *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 661 | −17 | −19 | 52% | −1.02 | −1.09 | 0.843 |
| 10-day | 661 |  +5 |  +3 | 54% | +0.22 | +0.26 | 0.415 |
| 20-day | 661 | +17 | +15 | 54% | +0.53 | +0.63 | 0.301 |
| 40-day | 660 | +59 | +57 | 54% | +1.32 | +1.63 | 0.093 |

**Nothing clears the bar.** The largest statistic anywhere is **HAC *t* = 1.63 at 40 days** — well
under the desk's **t ≥ 2** threshold — and at that horizon the small positive is indistinguishable
from holding the index for 40 days (the wave-1 direction is usually *up*, so a 40-day long is mostly
market beta, not an Elliott edge). At 5 days the "edge" is actually *negative*. The same-bars coin
placebo confirms it: a random direction at the identical swing points matches or beats the wave
count **30–84%** of the time. The wave count adds **no directional information** over a coin.

## The completed-impulse prediction — "sell the finished five-wave" (pooled)

The other forward-looking EW claim: after a completed five-wave impulse, a corrective move follows
*against* the impulse. We flag the 5th pivot (1,339 events) and bet against the impulse direction.

| horizon | n | mean (bps) | win-rate | one-sample *t* | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 1,339 |  +6 | 48% | +0.50 | +0.46 |
| 10-day | 1,339 | +15 | 48% | +0.96 | +0.83 |
| 20-day | 1,335 |  +8 | 46% | +0.35 | +0.26 |
| 40-day | 1,331 | −41 | 45% | −1.42 | −1.03 |

Again nothing significant — and at 40 days the "correction" bet is *losing* (the market keeps
drifting up after the impulse, the opposite of the prediction). The completed-impulse correction
claim is not supported either.

## Robustness — it fails the same way under every reasonable setting

**Fibonacci wave-2 band (H = 20):**

| band | n | mean (bps) | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| textbook 50–61.8% | 188 | +60 | 1.10 |
| wide 38.2–78.6% (headline) | 661 | +17 | 0.53 |
| deep 61.8–100% | 579 | −23 | −0.69 |

**ZigZag reversal threshold (H = 20):**

| threshold | n | mean (bps) | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 3% | 1,360 | −10 | −0.53 |
| 5% (headline) | 661 | +17 | +0.53 |
| 8% | 282 | +50 | +1.03 |

No setting reaches *t* = 2. The "textbook" tight 50–61.8% band gives the biggest point estimate
(+60 bps) but with only 188 events it is *t* = 1.10 — not significant, and exactly the kind of
narrow-sample number a believer would over-read. Tightening the ZigZag raises the per-trade size
but shrinks *n* and the *t* stays small. The conclusion is robust: **no edge at any sensible knob.**

## SPY-only — the named single tape (lower power, same answer)

| horizon | n | mean (bps) | win-rate | one-sample *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 67 | −10 | 54% | −0.18 | 0.571 |
| 10-day | 67 |  +3 | 58% | +0.04 | 0.486 |
| 20-day | 67 | +41 | 57% | +0.42 | 0.345 |
| 40-day | 67 | +15 | 54% | +0.12 | 0.464 |

SPY alone yields only 67 wave-3 entries over 33 years — far too few to certify anything — and shows
nothing. This is *why* we pool: even the higher-power pooled test finds no edge.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

On a deterministic panel where we **plant** a textbook impulse 1-2 followed by a known wave-3
extension (knob `edge`), the detector + inference behave exactly as they must (H = 10):

| planted edge | entries | mean (bps) | win-rate | one-sample *t* | HAC *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (pure random walk) | 83 | −35 | 48% | −0.97 | −0.92 | 0.810 |
| **+0.15** (planted wave-3) | 112 | +470 | 78% | **+7.02** | **+7.33** | **0.000** |

With **no** planted edge the wave-3 detector sits at *t* ≈ −1 (it does **not** manufacture
significance from a random walk); with a real planted wave-3 extension it lights up at **t = 7.02**,
placebo *p* = 0. The harness can clearly detect Elliott's predicted structure **when it is actually
there** — so the flat real-tape result is a true negative, not a broken pipeline.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The tightest mechanical Elliott rule — buy wave 3 after a Fibonacci-validated
  impulse 1-2 — produces **no** statistically detectable edge on the real tape: the largest
  statistic anywhere is **HAC *t* = 1.63 at 40 days** (where it's just market beta), every shorter
  horizon is noise or negative, and a same-bars coin matches it 30–84% of the time. Robust to the
  Fibonacci band and the ZigZag threshold; the completed-impulse "correction" claim fails too. A
  synthetic control proves the harness *would* catch a planted wave-3 (t = 7.02), so this is a
  genuine null. The method is also **irreducibly subjective** — even this generous mechanical proxy
  can't certify it, and a human "wave count" has far more degrees of freedom to fit in hindsight.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no edge to charge costs against. The one mildly-positive
  number (40-day) is indistinguishable from buying-and-holding the index, and costs make the fast
  versions negative. Nothing to deploy.
- **"Five waves predict the next move"? — NOT SUPPORTED.** Neither forward-looking EW prediction —
  wave-3 extension after a 1-2, nor a correction after a completed five-wave impulse — is
  distinguishable from chance on 33 years of broad-index daily data. Elliott Wave reads beautifully
  on a chart *after* the fact; out-of-sample, its mechanical core predicts nothing.
